A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe DoSAPP with the same authors, algorithm and core experiments. Both documents, including their appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and forgetting results across five datasets, an Aircraft-to-Cars sequence, component ablations and momentum sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original DoSAPP experiments and adds adaptation-method comparisons, corruption tests, controlled ablations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains gradient-selected sparse updates, teacher-student pseudo-label selection, accumulated task masks, dual-momentum EMA and the CLIP loss. v2 clarifies which parameters remain frozen. The mitigation strategies suggested in its limitations section are not presented as implemented method changes.

E1.justification: The five evaluated datasets, class-incremental sequences, Aircraft-to-Cars sequence and imbalanced-stream scenario remain. v2 adds Gaussian-corrupted CIFAR100 adaptation and evaluation scenarios (Table 9). Oxford Pets disappears from the dataset paragraph, but v1 contains no corresponding reported experiment establishing removed coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated SPU+Du, SPU+RMT and SparsCL+RMT comparisons (Table 4), plus FLYP, ZSCL, SLCA and SPU comparators within the existing imbalance experiment (Table 3). The standalone SL row disappears from Table 2. Finetune becoming FLYP is a matched rename, not a new baseline.

E3.justification: The reported forgetting metric changes from decline relative to accuracy immediately after learning each task to decline relative to its best earlier accuracy. v2 adds controlled data-fraction, sparsity, TTL-removal and full-test-set evaluations. Table 2 also changes the stated replay status of L2P, DualPrompt, SparseCL and SLCA to ER=1000; their unchanged scores do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls isolating dual momentum without mask union, teacher-only pseudo-labels and the TTL phase itself. New analyses examine corruption, unlabeled-data quantity, sparsity, per-task forgetting, evaluation-set choice and runtime (Table 6, Tables 9–16 and Figure 3). Momentum sensitivity and class imbalance were already studied in v1.

E5.justification: The uncertainty values accompanying long-sequence accuracies in v1 Table 3 disappear from v2 Table 5; for example, 45.01 ± 0.31 becomes 45.01. Both appendices retain averaging over five random seeds, so this is reduced uncertainty reporting, not evidence of fewer runs.

E6.justification: The main DoSAPP Table 2 scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial comparison and ablation results. Retained analyses also change numerically: momentum-table Aircraft accuracy changes from 39.40 to 39.14, and union-mask Aircraft accuracy from 32.99 to 31.79. The old SPU+ER scores reappear in v2 Table 15 under full-test evaluation, while Table 2 reports different subset-evaluation scores; these are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of forgetting changes substantively in the evaluation section, from post-learning-versus-final accuracy to best-previous-versus-final accuracy. The dual-momentum derivation is otherwise retained from Appendix A.1 as Appendix 8.1, without a new theorem or substantive proof revision.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains interleaving supervised learning with unlabeled deployment data to reduce forgetting without replay. v2 qualifies the novelty claim from being the first work to being among the early works and explicitly adds task-boundary-independent test-time operation to its contribution statements.

C2.justification: The mask-union interpretation changes from deterioration in v1 to generally beneficial effects except on Aircraft in v2. New discussions explain teacher-only pseudo-label staleness, sparse-capacity limits, adaptation to corruption and modest runtime savings. Appendix 8.4 expands limitations concerning extreme skew and partial task coverage and proposes untested mitigations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies an equal split between adaptation and evaluation data and clarifies candidate versus permanently frozen parameters. The reported hardware changes from NVIDIA A100 to V100, and the approximate one-hour runtime statement is replaced by per-task timing comparisons. The principal hyperparameter table remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against TTA and CTTA through Table 1 and rewritten related work, including NOTE, EATA, EcoTTA, RMT, PSMT and DSS. It also directly distinguishes DoSAPP from Chen et al. (2025) using the claimed absence of required task-boundary information. These are substantive positioning changes beyond bibliography formatting.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Results becomes a separate section, while limitations and the momentum discussion move into the appendix. This is substantial editorial restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds a CTTA comparison matrix, numerous experimental tables and a three-panel forgetting heatmap. Existing tables are reorganized: replay groups change, the long-sequence table gains a forgetting column, and imbalance results become a separate comparison table. The original two schematics are retained, with Figure 2 relocated, within a substantially revised journal layout.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's validation by isolating the contribution of TTL and pseudo-label selection and comparing against CL methods combined with test-time adaptation (Tables 4 and 12–14). Together with corruption and sensitivity analyses, these controls substantially strengthen support for the central retention mechanism. These gains outweigh the removed long-sequence uncertainty values and remaining reporting problems, including the inconsistent forgetting-sign explanation in Appendix 8.7.
